pr_title: x-pack/plugin/apm-data: add dynamic setting for enabling template registry
pr_body:
Add `xpack.apm_data.registry.enabled` cluster setting, which can be used to disable the index template registry while restoring a snapshot.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104385
pr_comments: Hi @axw, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Thanks @danielmitterdorfer, apparently I forgot to run all the tests after making the latest change :man_facepalming:
Now explicitly enabling the registry in the `@Before`.

issue_context.title: x-pack/plugin/apm-data: support dynamically enabling registry
issue_context.body:
### Description

We need to support dynamically enabling/disabling the apm-data index template registry, to support restoring a cluster from a snapshot. Basically we'll need to support what is described fro Universal Profiling here: https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/master/snapshots-restore-snapshot.html#restore-entire-cluster
comments: Currently there's just one setting, `xpack.apm_data.enabled`, which enables/disables the plugin. This setting is not dynamic. Can we make that dynamic, and have it control the registry? Or do we need a new setting?

review_comments: We tend to encapsulate this in the code of the class using the `enabled` flag, in this case the `APMIndexTemplateRegistry`. We usually read the value of the setting and we set it in the constructor and in a method like `initialize()` we register the listener. This way it's transparent in the `APMIndexTemplateRegistry` how the enabled flag is changing.

@gmarouli is it worth me changing now? I can go back and update it.

The only way the `enabled` flag is updated is through the `setEnabled` method, and I'm not sure why `APMIndexTemplateRegistry` would care what caused that method to be called -- but if it's conventional and this difference will be confusing, I can go back and update it.
It's more about encapsulation, the logic of how the flag for this class is changing is contained in the class itself. It's ok for now, if we come back to this we can address it.
Just as a suggestion: If you want to be extra cautious you could also add a test to ensure the registry is disabled if the plugin is disabled.
